title: Hypothesis-to-Acceptance Pathway: Quarterly Roadmap for Enterprise On‑Prem Features
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: This ticket defines a repeatable hypothesis-to-acceptance pathway for quarterly planning of enterprise on-prem/VPC features. Goal is to reduce cycle time from idea to customer-accepted production delivery while preserving security and interoperability checks. It unifies experiments, acceptance criteria, telemetry signals, and OKR mapping so each feature rollout has a clear ‘what success looks like’ and fallback plan.
objectives_and_key_results_map: OKR-PRIV-1: Decrease private activation time for new customers by 40% (KR: onboarding checklist automation)
OKR-PRIV-2: Maintain 99.9% SLA for dedicated on-prem endpoints post-rollout
OKR-DEV-3: Reduce mean time-to-detect deployment regressions by 50% via rollout telemetry
acceptance_criteria: Automated compatibility test-suite passes for supported OS/container versions on customer-shaped lab images
Deployment runbook executed end-to-end in staging with <10 manual steps and documented exceptions
Telemetry (activation latency, error-rate, CPU/GPU utilization) meets the defined SLO targets in staging for two 72h windows
Customer validation checklist completed by solutions engineering for two pilot tenants and signed off
Security checklist (KMS integration, audit-log streaming, RBAC) marked as green in security audit
milestones: 2026-03-18: Hypothesis board finalized and prioritized (owner: PM)
2026-04-05: Technical spike & compatibility matrix completed (owner: Eng)
2026-05-25: Acceptance sign-off and launch window decision (owner: PM)
risks: Vendor kernel differences across customer environments may cause flaking compatibility tests
Long lead times for customer security reviews can delay pilot sign-off
Autoscaling behavior in low-latency edge pockets could diverge from cloud metrics, masking regressions
Rollout may expose emergent telemetry that requires a change to runtime kernels, introducing additional eng work
decision_log: 2026-03-11: Decided to prioritize compatibility-by-sample over attempting to cover all OS permutations; we will maintain lab images matching top 20 enterprise environments
2026-03-12: Chose a two-wave pilot (internal + 2 customers) rather than a broad dark-launch to limit blast radius
2026-03-12: Agreed fallback: if staging error-rate > 0.5% for 24h, automatically roll traffic to hosted fallback variant
updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket created after leadership sync; initial scope covers onboarding automation + acceptance bar for private/VPC installs
2026-03-11: Eng spike scoped to 5 days; estimated work for kernel compatibility prototypes; ENG-2042 added as dependency
2026-03-12: Security reviewed the initial checklist and flagged KMS integration for early gating; security_review_required set to true
2026-03-12: Solutions Eng identified two anchor customers willing to pilot in April; added to milestone plan
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: narrower lab-image coverage accelerates time-to-pilot but accepts residual customer-specific edge cases; mitigation: fast-track per-customer compatibility fixes via dedicated escalation lane
Tradeoff: two-wave pilot reduces risk but increases time-to-wide-activation; mitigation: clear criteria for when to move from pilot->ramp
Decision: postpone full autoscaler policy integration until after acceptance window to avoid conflating rollout regressions with autoscaler instability
post_release_signals: Customer support ticket volume for pilot customers
